name: manual_dc0f92
claim: When a wrapper/delegator refactor lands (an old module replaced by a thin re-export shim around a new canonical implementation), every stale branch that predates the refactor is at risk of the same failure mode in every file that got wrapped -- not just the one file where it was first noticed. Finding one instance of a branch's file being a superseded pre-refactor copy is a signal to explicitly check every other file the same refactor touched, not just the one that happened to surface via a conflict or a test failure.

decisions.notes: The same structural-supersession pattern recurred three times in one merge before being generalized -- worth capturing as 'check the whole refactor' once recognized, not just the one file.

rationale: The same structural-supersession pattern recurred three times in one merge before being generalized -- worth capturing as 'check the whole refactor' once recognized, not just the one file.
